Most visitors sleep in Namba and never see where Osaka actually lives. These two neighbourhoods are a short ride from the centre, with cheaper dinners, lantern-lit bars full of office workers, and quiet mornings 👇

📍 TENMA
1 stop from Osaka Station on the JR Loop Line

🛍️ Japan's longest covered shopping street runs right through it. Tenjinbashisuji is 2.6 km long, with about 600 shops selling croquettes, fish, pickles and old-school coffee.

🏮 Just north of JR Tenma are the Ura-Tenma alleys: tiny izakaya under hundreds of lanterns, about 5 minutes on foot.

🍻 It's lively at night, but local-lively. Office workers and neighbours, not tour groups.

🚇 Getting around: the JR Loop Line takes you to Osaka Station for Kyoto trains, the airport express and Universal Studios. The Sakaisuji Line reaches Nipponbashi in about 10 minutes.

📍 TSURUHASHI
Osaka's Korean neighbourhood

🥩 Famous for yakiniku. The market lanes start the moment you step out of the station.

🚶 Miyuki-dori Koreatown is a 10–15 minute walk south.

🦌 Kintetsu trains to Nara stop here, and the Sennichimae Line runs direct to Namba. A smart base if Nara is on your list.

✅ OUR TAKE

First trip, two or three nights? Stay central. It saves time.

Second trip, four nights or more, or going mainly for the food? Tenma or Tsuruhashi gives you everyday Osaka.

👉 Full guide with lines, walking times and hotels:
https://japanbystation.com/osaka-live-like-a-local

Hotel breakfast, or breakfast where Osaka's restaurant chefs buy their fish? On one morning of your trip, it's worth swapping. Here's a 300-year-old working market one subway stop from the centre, and exactly when to go 👇

Hotel breakfasts are comfortable, and on most mornings that's exactly what you want.

But you can have scrambled eggs anywhere in the world. This one you can only have in Osaka.

🏮 KIZU WHOLESALE MARKET

More than 300 years of history. Every morning, chefs from Osaka's restaurants come here for fish, vegetables and dried goods.

Visitors can walk in and buy too.

It's quieter and less polished than the famous markets. No crowds of tour groups, just a working market getting on with its day. That's exactly why we love it.

🚇 HOW TO GET THERE

Osaka Metro Midosuji or Yotsubashi Line to Daikokucho.

Take Exit 1. It's about 3 minutes on foot.

⏰ WHEN TO GO

Best between 8:30 and 10:30.

Stalls open around dawn for the chefs, and many close by late morning, so don't sleep in.

Closed Sundays, national holidays, some Wednesdays, and 31 Dec – 4 Jan. Check the calendar on kizu-ichiba.com the night before.

🍣 HOW WE'D SPEND THAT MORNING

1️⃣ Skip the buffet, just for this one day.

2️⃣ Ride the subway to Daikokucho.

3️⃣ Walk the aisles slowly and watch the market at work.

4️⃣ Sit down to a seafood bowl.

5️⃣ Head back into the city with the whole day ahead of you, and a breakfast you'll actually remember.

➕ TWO MORE LOCAL MARKETS

🥩 Tsuruhashi Market: covered lanes right outside Tsuruhashi Station, full of yakiniku, Korean grocers and fish stalls. Come hungry in the evening, and bring cash.

🛍️ Tenjinbashisuji: a 2.6 km covered shopping street locals use every day. About 40 minutes end to end, and lovely when it rains.

👉 All three markets and the best time for each:
https://japanbystation.com/osaka-local-markets

Would you give up one hotel breakfast for this? 👇

We priced the same three nights on both sides of Osaka Station. Walking 12 minutes saved ¥9,474. Here's when that walk is worth it, and when it isn't 👇

It's one of the most common Osaka booking questions: pay more to sleep right at the station, or walk a little and keep the money?

📅 Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, 1 adult, Booking.com, checked 23 Nov.

💰 THE PRICES

🏨 Hotel Monterey Osaka, about 400 m from Osaka Station: ¥34,394 for 3 nights.

🌿 Quintessa Hotel Osaka Umeda, about 400 m from Nakazakicho Station, double room, rated 8.5: ¥24,920 for 3 nights.

That's about ¥3,160 a night less, or ¥9,474 over the stay.

🚶 THE CATCH

It's about 800 m, roughly 12 minutes on foot, from Osaka Station.

Add a few minutes to get from your platform to the street. Osaka Station is big, and first-timers often underestimate it.

Rather not walk? Nakazakicho is one stop from Higashi-Umeda on the Tanimachi subway line.

✅ OUR TAKE

👜 Small bag: walk it. You'll be walking to Umeda most days anyway.

🧳 Heavy suitcase: still book Nakazakicho, and take a taxi on arrival and departure only. Osaka taxis start at ¥600, the ride is about 6 minutes, so expect ¥600–800 each way. You still keep around ¥7,900.

🚄 Early trains most mornings: then the hotel on top of the station is worth it. Hotel Granvia Osaka is about 100 m from the platforms, but it was ¥49,243 for the same three nights.

📏 ONE RULE OF THUMB

Check the gap on your own dates. If it drops below about ¥500 a night, the two taxis cancel out the saving. Book in Umeda.

👉 Full price check, route and taxi fares:
https://japanbystation.com/nakazakicho-vs-umeda-hotel

Walk, taxi, or pay for the station hotel? 👇

Booking an apartment for your group in Osaka? The city stopped accepting new special-zone rental applications on 29 May 2026 and is inspecting rentals more closely, so unlicensed listings can be cancelled at short notice. Here's the 3-step check we'd do before paying 👇

⚠️ IS IT LEGAL?

Short-term rentals in Japan need a registration or a special-zone certification.

Legal hosts must record your passport at check-in.

✅ OUR 3-STEP CHECK

1️⃣ Find the registration or certification number on the listing. No number, no booking.

2️⃣ Expect a passport check. A host who never asks for ID is a warning sign.

3️⃣ Add cleaning fees and taxes for every night before you compare with hotel rooms.

🏠 PRIVATE APARTMENT

Good: one shared living space, a kitchen, a washing machine.

Watch: often one bathroom for four, cleaning fees, self check-in, and some have a minimum stay.

🏨 APARTMENT HOTEL

Good: real beds for four, a kitchenette, a laundry machine, and staff if something goes wrong.

Watch: popular with groups, so they book out early.

🛏️ TWO TWIN ROOMS

Good: two bathrooms, daily cleaning, easy cancellation, often right by the station.

Watch: rooms are compact, and there's no common space to hang out.

✅ OUR TAKE

Two or three nights: two twin rooms near a station are usually the easiest.

Four nights or more: an apartment hotel often wins, because laundry and a living room start to matter.

👉 Full comparison:
https://japanbystation.com/osaka-four-friends

Save this for your group chat 📌

#osakatrip #grouptravel #osaka #japantravel

Landing at Narita, three nights in Tokyo, then the bullet train to Kyoto? Where you sleep decides two journeys: the one in and the one out. 🚄

We priced the same three nights (Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, two adults, Booking.com) at the three stations people usually pick.

━━━━━━━━━━
📍 1. UENO
━━━━━━━━━━

Our pick for most trips.

• Skyliner from Narita to Keisei Ueno in as little as 41 minutes, ¥2,470
• Three nights for two from about ¥41,000 (well-rated hotels within 400 m)
• Ueno to Kyoto took 2 h 28 min on our sample morning, with one change at Tokyo Station

Keisei Ueno and JR Ueno are separate stations, about 9 minutes apart on foot. Book on the Keisei side if you can.

━━━━━━━━━━
📍 2. TOKYO STATION
━━━━━━━━━━

The Shinkansen starts here, so departure morning is easy.

• N'EX from Narita in 53 minutes at its fastest, ¥3,140
• The 9:00 Nozomi reached Kyoto at 11:15, no change
• But three nights cost from about ¥84,000, roughly double Ueno

━━━━━━━━━━
📍 3. SHINAGAWA
━━━━━━━━━━

The quiet winner for west-side itineraries.

• N'EX continues here: 71 minutes on our sample train, ¥3,330
• The same Nozomi stops 7 minutes after Tokyo: 2 h 8 min to Kyoto
• Shibuya is 13 minutes away on the Yamanote Line
• Three nights from about ¥59,000

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ OUR TAKE
━━━━━━━━━━

Ueno saved about ¥40,000 over three nights against Tokyo Station, for about 13 extra minutes on one morning. Book Shinagawa if two or more of your days are around Shibuya and Harajuku. Pay for Tokyo Station only with very heavy bags or a very early train.

Full guide with hotel names and the departure-day timings 👉 https://japanbystation.com/narita-three-nights-then-shinkansen

Which would you pick: cheaper nights or the easier last morning? 👇

One mistake we see on Tokyo-then-Kyoto trips: paying Tokyo Station prices for every night, just to save one morning. 🧳

━━━━━━━━━━
❌ THE MISTAKE
━━━━━━━━━━

Booking three nights by Tokyo Station "because the Shinkansen leaves from there".

On our sample dates (Mon 14 – Thu 17 Dec 2026, two adults), well-rated rooms within 700 m of Tokyo Station started around ¥84,000 for the three nights. That is about ¥28,000 or more a night.

━━━━━━━━━━
⏱️ WHAT IT ACTUALLY SAVES
━━━━━━━━━━

• Tokyo Station to Kyoto by Nozomi: 2 h 15 min
• Ueno to Kyoto, with one change at Tokyo: 2 h 28 min
• Shinagawa to Kyoto, on the same Nozomi: 2 h 8 min

So the expensive base saves about 13 minutes against Ueno, once. Shinagawa is actually 7 minutes quicker than Tokyo Station.

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ THE FIX
━━━━━━━━━━

• Sleep in Ueno for the cheap nights (three nights from about ¥41,000 on the same dates)
• Or Shinagawa if your days are on the west side (Shibuya is 13 minutes away)
• Only if you need a no-change, walk-to-the-platform morning, move to Tokyo Station for the last night only

━━━━━━━━━━
💡 ONE MORE THING
━━━━━━━━━━

Arriving at Narita? The Skyliner reaches Keisei Ueno in as little as 41 minutes. The Narita Express goes to Tokyo Station and on to Shinagawa. Match your hotel to your airport train, not just to the bullet train.

The full comparison, with hotel names and prices 👉 https://japanbystation.com/narita-three-nights-then-shinkansen

Save this for when you book your Tokyo nights. 📌

Landing at Haneda at 11 p.m.? You are racing the last trains, and some areas are already out of reach. ✈️

Here is what we found for a weekday night (Wed 16 Dec 2026), arriving at Terminal 3.

━━━━━━━━━━
🚆 1. THE TRAIN, IF YOU ARE OUT FAST
━━━━━━━━━━

After immigration, bags and customs, we plan on reaching arrivals at about 23:45 at best.

• Asakusa: last train 23:37, usually missed
• Shinjuku and Shibuya: 23:51 via Shinagawa, tight
• Hamamatsucho, Tokyo Station, Ueno: the Tokyo Monorail at 00:10

A Hamamatsucho hotel is the safest central pick: the Monorail ends there at 00:26, no change.

━━━━━━━━━━
🚕 2. NIGHT BUS OR TAXI
━━━━━━━━━━

• Late-night Limousine Bus at 0:20, 1:00, 1:40 and 2:20 to Shinjuku, Higashi-shinjuku and Ikebukuro, ¥2,800
• Fixed-fare taxi with the 20% night premium: about ¥9,800 to Shinjuku, plus tolls
• Two people sharing: roughly ¥5,000 each, door to door

━━━━━━━━━━
🏨 3. SLEEP AT THE AIRPORT
━━━━━━━━━━

• Villa Fontaine Grand Haneda Airport is connected to Terminal 3, with a 24-hour front desk
• About ¥18,700 for two that night
• Comparable central rooms were about ¥19,200–19,900 the same night
• First trains into the city leave at about 5:26

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ OUR TAKE
━━━━━━━━━━

With checked bags and a 23:00 landing, sleep at the airport on night one. It costs about the same as town and skips a ¥10,000 taxi. Go straight in only with hand luggage and a Monorail-side hotel, or a hotel on the night-bus route.

Full guide with every last train 👉 https://japanbystation.com/haneda-late-arrival-first-night

What time does your flight land? 👇

Save this before a late flight into Haneda. A five-step checklist we use for anything landing after 10 p.m. 📌

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ 1. CHECK YOUR LANDING TIME AGAINST THE LAST TRAIN
━━━━━━━━━━

From Terminal 3 on a weekday:

• Asakusa: 23:37
• Shinjuku, Shibuya, Shinagawa: 23:51
• Hamamatsucho, Tokyo Station, Ueno: 00:10 (Tokyo Monorail)

Add time for immigration and bags. We assume arrivals at about 23:45 at best for a 23:00 landing.

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ 2. CHECK YOUR HOTEL'S FRONT DESK
━━━━━━━━━━

Arriving at 1 a.m.? Make sure the listing says 24-hour front desk, or tell the hotel you will be late.

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ 3. KNOW THE NIGHT BUS
━━━━━━━━━━

• Airport Limousine late-night buses: 0:20, 1:00, 1:40, 2:20
• To Shinjuku Station West Exit, Busta Shinjuku, Higashi-shinjuku and Ikebukuro
• ¥2,800 per person

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ 4. PRICE THE TAXI FOR YOUR GROUP
━━━━━━━━━━

• Haneda fixed fares add a 20% premium from 22:00 to 5:00
• About ¥9,800 to Shinjuku, ¥9,200 to Shibuya, ¥9,900 to Ueno or Asakusa
• Tolls are extra, about ¥1,000
• Worth it for two to four people; less so alone

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ 5. COMPARE THE AIRPORT HOTEL
━━━━━━━━━━

On Wed 16 Dec 2026, Villa Fontaine Grand Haneda Airport, connected to Terminal 3, was about ¥18,700 for two. Central business hotels were about the same. If the numbers match, the airport night wins.

Our rule of thumb: land after about 22:30 with checked bags, sleep at the airport and ride in from 5:26 the next morning.

All the times and prices in one place 👉 https://japanbystation.com/haneda-late-arrival-first-night

Send this to whoever you are flying with. ✈️

"Five minutes from Shinjuku Station." With a suitcase, from your actual train, it can be closer to twenty. 🧳

We traced one real hotel that says this: Hotel Gracery Shinjuku in Kabukicho, "5 minutes from JR Shinjuku's East Exit".

━━━━━━━━━━
🚆 1. FROM THE NARITA EXPRESS
━━━━━━━━━━

• Our sample N'EX: Narita 15:14, Shinjuku 16:41, ¥3,330
• It stops at platforms 5–6
• JR East says the lift route from there leads to the New South, Koshu-kaido and Miraina Tower gates: the south end
• The hotel is at the north end, about 970 m away on the street
• With bags, we budget 15–20 minutes to reception (on the 8th floor)

━━━━━━━━━━
🚇 2. FROM THE ADVERTISED EXIT
━━━━━━━━━━

• From the JR East Exit plaza it really is about 470 m, around 6 minutes
• Step-free option: Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line lifts from the East Gate to Exit B11 or A6
• Those lifts run 6:00–23:00 only
• Exit B11 to the hotel: about 450 m

━━━━━━━━━━
🚌 3. FROM THE AIRPORT BUS
━━━━━━━━━━

• Narita Limousine Bus straight to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower, ¥3,600
• 115 minutes on our sample timetable, about 30 minutes slower than N'EX
• But the stop is only about 200 m from the hotel door

━━━━━━━━━━
✅ OUR TAKE
━━━━━━━━━━

Always check which exit the "minutes" are counted from. For a Kabukicho hotel with a big suitcase, take the bus when one leaves within about 30 minutes of clearing customs; otherwise take N'EX and allow 15–20 minutes. If your hotel is near the South Exit or Busta Shinjuku, the N'EX lift route ends right there and the train wins.

Full trace with every distance 👉 https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-five-minutes-with-a-suitcase

Has a "5 minutes from the station" hotel ever surprised you? 👇

Big suitcase, Narita, hotel in Shinjuku. Which would you take? 🤔

━━━━━━━━━━
🅰️ THE NARITA EXPRESS
━━━━━━━━━━

• 87 minutes on our sample train, ¥3,330
• Arrives at platforms 5–6 at JR Shinjuku
• The lift route from those platforms comes out at the south gates (New South, Koshu-kaido, Miraina Tower)

Great if your hotel is on the south side. Hotel Sunroute Plaza Shinjuku, for example, says 3 minutes from the South Exit.

For a hotel on the north side, the walk from the south gates is about 970 m before you count the station itself.

━━━━━━━━━━
🅱️ THE LIMOUSINE BUS
━━━━━━━━━━

• Narita to Tokyu Kabukicho Tower: 115 minutes on our sample timetable, ¥3,600
• About 30 minutes slower and ¥270 more than the train
• Drops you about 200 m from north-side hotels such as Hotel Gracery Shinjuku

Great with heavy bags, kids or tired legs. Not so great if the next bus is an hour away.

━━━━━━━━━━
💡 HOW WE DECIDE
━━━━━━━━━━

• Find which exit your hotel's "minutes" are counted from
• Hotel near the South Exit or Busta Shinjuku: take A
• Hotel on the north side with a big case and a bus within about 30 minutes: take B
• No bus soon: take A and budget 15–20 minutes from platform to reception

One extra tip: if you come in on the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line, its lifts from the East Gate up to Exits B11 and A6 run from 6:00 to 23:00. Late at night, expect stairs.

The full trace, with each distance 👉 https://japanbystation.com/shinjuku-five-minutes-with-a-suitcase

A or B for your trip? 👇
